published_statement: NOT QUOTED -- the source was not read (see source.via). The tree's form (branelink.py:38-39): single-mode capacity ceiling I_dot <= sqrt(pi P/(3 hbar))/ln 2 bits/s, i.e. S_dot <= sqrt(pi k_B^2 P/(3 hbar)) in entropy units. Re-derived here (not read): for one unidirectional mode in a thermal state, P = pi k^2 T^2/(12 hbar), S_dot = pi k^2 T/(6 hbar), so S_dot^2/P = pi k^2/(3 hbar) exactly, and thermal occupation maximises S_dot at fixed P.
published_hypotheses: NOT QUOTED from source (unread). The hypotheses under which THIS AUDIT re-derived the form, each NAMED:
H1 one channel = one transverse mode, 1+1 propagation, unidirectional, reflectionless (search summary (a) corroborates 'per channel', not verbatim)
H2 free (non-interacting) mode; energy flux measured from the band bottom (or from mu for a Fermi sea); zero-point flux excluded

H3 dispersion w(k) monotone onto [0, inf) -- the 'field-blind' (dispersion-independent) clause; a bounded band or a counted rest energy gives a strictly lower achievable ratio, so the ceiling still bounds

H4 stationary state; information rate identified with entropy rate, which needs an ideal noiseless receiver (capacity via Holevo -- per summary (b), Caves-Drummond for bosons, Blencowe-Vitelli for any statistics; not read)
hypothesis_drift: UNVERIFIABLE AGAINST SOURCE: the source is unread, so no drift from Pendry's own hypotheses is asserted. The drifts below are measured against the re-derived form (H1-H4), and every one concerns the O6/O7 pass's use that branelink.py itself REFUSES.

branelink.py:38-42 -- 'field-blind' carried to 'a carrier with gamma > 1 on a moving brane': ADDED a frame change. Computed here (checks 5a-5c): for a unidirectional MASSLESS 1+1 flux S_dot^2/P is Doppler-invariant (S' = D S, P' = D^2 P), so a boost alone does not move the ceiling; for a massive carrier the frame behaviour was NOT computed here and stays a named gap.

branelink.py:38-42 -- '... in a 5D bulk': DROPS H1 (single mode). A bulk degree of freedom seen from the brane is a tower/continuum of modes; computed here (6a, 6b): N channels at total P have ceiling sqrt(N) x the single-mode ceiling, and no split beats the equal one. The single-mode ceiling is therefore NOT a field-blind ceiling for a bulk carrier unless the number of accessible modes is counted -- this supports the tree's refusal (failure mode (4)).

branelink.py:39 'capacity ceiling' -- silently includes H4 (information = entropy, ideal receiver); the O6 pass pairs it with a LIGO-class receiver (branelink.py:31-33), which is far from ideal: the ceiling bounds, it does not estimate.

Statistics -- neither the tree nor the pass states it. Computed here (4b, 4b', 4c): a fermionic Fermi-sea channel (electrons and holes) SATURATES the same ceiling; a particles-only band with bottom at mu reaches 1/sqrt(2) of it. The auditor's first-run expectation (pi/6 for the Fermi sea) was WRONG and is recorded in the script; the ceiling remains an upper bound in every case tested.

branelink.py:350 (S5 N(A)) -- no drift: sqrt(A pi/(3 hbar ln^2 2)) is identically sqrt(pi A/(3 hbar))/ln 2 (check 7); what the tree refuses at S5 is the round-trip A(N(A)) = A as evidence, not the formula.

data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: NO. Computed (check 8): ceiling at P = 1 W moves from 1.437631e17 to 1.437642e17 bit/s, relative 8.0e-6. The form S_dot^2/P = pi k^2/(3 hbar) is a theorem of quantum statistics under H1-H4 and carries no fitted or measured input beyond hbar.

rederivation.outcome: 27/27 PASS (sympy + scipy quadrature). (1) 1D thermal boson flux: P = pi T^2/12 (Gamma(2)zeta(2), cross-checked by quadrature), S_dot = pi T/6, S_dot^2/P = pi/3 -> sqrt(pi P/(3 hbar)) in nats. (2) Thermal is the maximiser: the stationary point of s(n) - beta w n is Bose-Einstein and s(n) is strictly concave (symbolic); 400 random non-thermal spectra reach at most 0.9226 of the ceiling. (3) Dispersion-blind: w = c|k|, k^2, k^3 and sqrt(k^2+m^2)-m all give pi/3 to <=5e-9; a bounded band gives ratio < 1 at every finite T with sup 1 as T -> 0 (0.998 at T = 0.2 W, 0.327 at T = 50 W); rest energy counted in P caps at 0.9339. (4) Fermions: Fermi sea (e+h) saturates pi/3; particles-only with band bottom at mu gives pi/6 (1/sqrt 2), best over mu 0.7071 at mu = 0. (5) Doppler: for a unidirectional massless flux S_dot^2/P is boost-invariant. (6) N modes at total P: sqrt(N) x single ceiling. (7) branelink N(A) identical to the ceiling in bits. (8) hbar then/now: 8.0e-6 relative. (9) dP/dT = pi^2 k^2 T/(3h), the single-channel thermal-conductance quantum. Two first-run failures (3b grid test; 4b expected pi/6) were the AUDITOR's errors, recorded in the script's comments and corrected by quadrature/derivation -- not findings about the source.

lacked_data: What Pendry (1983) did not have: (i) measurements of the single-channel thermal-conductance quantum -- phonons (Schwab et al. 2000), photons (Meschke et al. 2006), electrons (Jezouin et al. 2013), per titles only; (ii) a proof that the entropy ceiling is also the Holevo capacity (Caves-Drummond 1994 for bosons; Blencowe-Vitelli 2000 for any statistics; per search summaries); (iii) the post-2019 exact hbar. EVIDENCE EITHER WAY: (iii) is computed to move the ceiling by 8.0e-6 relative -- nothing; (i) and (ii), as far as the summaries go, CONFIRM rather than narrow, and this audit's own derivation reproduces the energy-flux quantum (check 9) that (i) measured. The result is a theorem of quantum statistics under H1-H4 with hbar as its only datum, so it is not the kind of result that later data overturns. M's hypothesis is therefore NOT supported for this result on the evidence gathered -- with the caveat that the source and the later papers were not read verbatim. What the tree's refused use lacks is not data but a HYPOTHESIS: a bulk carrier is not a single mode (check 6: sqrt(N) scaling), and a massive carrier's frame behaviour was not computed. Those are named gaps in the USE, not errors in the source.
grade_evidence: The source (Pendry 1983) and every restatement (Blencowe-Vitelli quant-ph/0001007, Bekenstein-Schiffer 1990) were unreachable this stage (alphaXiv quota; arxiv/iop/osti/S2/researchgate EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the published statement and hypotheses cannot be quoted and hypothesis drift cannot be measured against the source -- by M's rule that is OPEN, not STANDS. What IS established here, by computation (27/27 PASS): the formula as the tree writes it follows exactly from single-mode quantum statistics under named H1-H4; it is dispersion-blind (4 dispersions to <=5e-9) and remains an upper bound for bounded bands, counted rest energy and both fermion cases; it is Doppler-invariant for a unidirectional massless flux; its only datum (hbar) has moved 8.0e-6 relative; and it is NOT field-blind across mode count -- N modes carry sqrt(N) times the single-mode ceiling -- which is exactly why the tree's refusal to transport it to a 5D-bulk carrier (branelink.py:38-42, failure mode (4)) is sound. No counterexample to the single-mode statement was found; nothing here is WRONG.
